answer: To forge one identity an attacker must first own a grain elevator: buy one on the mesa-top wheat belt, pass inspection, post a 2,000-unit bond and wait 120 days. Registered under the agent's key, it backs exactly one identity; a second claim on the same elevator is rejected. Intakes are graded by kernel sample and logged, so a paper elevator earns nothing. Cheapest cheat: rent a licence — the lender surrenders the licence backing their own identity and risks a fraud charge, and a forgery fails the check at the harbor terminal. One hundred fakes need 100 elevators, 200,000 units, 12,000 days.
